summary: Login regression re-test. CRITICAL: The user's claim that 'DB has been RESET so all seeded accounts use original credentials' is FALSE. Direct MongoDB inspection shows the previous test run's mutations are still persisted: (1) admin siya@erank.co.za password hash does NOT verify against 'erank2026' (returns 401), (2) owner/marshal/driver seeded accounts still have must_change=False (should be True per spec). Passenger Lizwi Lakhe works correctly. Passenger self-register + change-secret + re-login flow works. Root cause: seed.py _upsert_user only updates non-secret fields on existing users — it does NOT rewrite secret_hash or must_change. So a plain re-seed cannot 'reset' credentials; the users collection must be dropped (or the specific fields explicitly reset) before re-seeding.

critical.issue: admin siya@erank.co.za / erank2026 returns 401 'Wrong details'. Stored bcrypt hash $2b$12$bxHHEaMFWDFb4Qc.MvrvSe... does NOT verify against 'erank2026' (or any obvious variant). Previous automated test's password change was never rolled back. User is locked out of admin.

Login SUCCEEDS with seeded PINs (123456 / 123456789 / 12345678) but response returns must_change=False for all three. Per spec these seeded non-passenger accounts must have must_change=True. Previous test mutated must_change and re-seed did not reset it. First-login change flow is now silently skipped for these accounts.

action_items: Reset admin siya@erank.co.za password_hash to bcrypt('erank2026') directly in MongoDB, OR drop the users collection and re-run seed. Do the same for the other 4 admins if their hashes also drift.

Reset must_change=True on all non-passenger seeded accounts (admin/owner/marshal/driver) — one-shot Mongo update: db.users.update_many({role:{$in:['admin','owner','marshal','driver']}}, {$set:{must_change:True}}). Note the specific 4 accounts under test are Mzamo Vilakazi, Muzi Sogoni, Sizwe Dlomo (plus siya) — but per spec ALL seeded non-passenger accounts should be True.

Enhance seed.py _upsert_user so a fresh seed run can idempotently restore the initial secret_hash and must_change (e.g. accept a `force_reset` flag, or add a one-shot admin endpoint / CLI to reset seeded credentials). Currently _upsert_user's line 84-87 branch never touches secret_hash/must_change on existing docs, which is why the user's 'DB reset' didn't take effect.

rca of the issue: Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/login {role:'admin',identifier:'siya@erank.co.za',secret:'erank2026'} -> 401. (2) Direct Mongo query on users collection: siya's secret_hash is $2b$12$bxHHEaMFWDFb4Qc.MvrvSe... which verify_secret('erank2026', hash) returns False. Root cause: previous automated test called /api/auth/change-secret against seeded admin, which overwrote secret_hash and set must_change=False. The user's claimed 'DB reset' did not drop the users collection, and seed._upsert_user's existing-user branch (seed.py:85-87) intentionally does NOT rewrite secret_hash or must_change — so re-running seed had no effect on already-mutated auth fields. Mitigation: (a) drop db.users then re-seed, OR (b) directly bcrypt-set siya.secret_hash to 'erank2026' and $set must_change:True on admin/owner/marshal/driver seeded rows. Long-term: add a reset flag / admin CLI so operators can restore seeded credentials without manual Mongo access.
